limitations: The structured world is built to reward reuse, and the ladder was designed knowing the arithmetic family; an automatic curriculum is a stronger test, which LA-015 attempts.
Goals are 8-bit functions and solutions are mostly known constant multiplications, so this is not new mathematics.
Sealed goals derive from public seeds so a reviewer can regenerate them, unlike a private NC-061 commitment.
The separate evaluator matches a canonical ISA program in tests but expressions are not compiled to ISA programs.
Library capped at 48 concepts, and CPU was measured under shared load.
Seed 19's structured library reaches 1.0 while the others stay near 0.3, so the mean is seed-dependent.
Structured gains of 0.233 and 0.367 are refused by the 0.95 retention floor and stand as NO_IMPROVEMENT.
Curriculum IMPROVEMENT is a one-time gain from 0 to about 0.21 on a hard family after training on an easier ladder; generation-to-generation gains do not compound.
All curriculum solve counts in the random arm are 0 of 30 per seed, so the size of the advantage has a coarse floor.
Runs shared the machine under heavy load, about 2x core count, so CPU figures are noisy.
Search fits 64 probes; every accepted solution is then checked on all 65,536 pairs by each of two separately written evaluators.
